title: Weekly microcredit top-up with conditional lockout + enterprise SQ contract language
creator: Leah Park
description:
Hypothesis: Moving from a one-time trial credit grant to a modest weekly microcredit top-up (e.g., 1,000 tokens/week for 6 weeks) with an abuse-protecting conditional lockout will increase mid-funnel activation and long-tail engagement, while reducing upfront cost and making upgrade prompts more contextually timed. For enterprise prospects, offer an extended trial credit package tied to completed security questionnaire (SQ) + conditional contractual language to accelerate sales cycles without exposing the company to uncontrolled free usage.

Key elements:
- Product change: implement weekly credit top-up for free accounts (configurable duration and amount).
- Abuse control: conditional lockout rules (suspicious traffic, automated scraping, sustained high throughput) that pause top-ups and require human review.
- Upgrade UX: timed CTAs in Console and API responses showing remaining weekly credits, projected runway, and one-click upgrade modal with price anchors.
- Communications: drip emails + in-console banners timed to top-up and exhaustion events.
- Enterprise path: sample contractual clause and SQ gating that allows Sales to request a 30-day boosted credit tranche when SQ completed.

Why different from prior tests: previous experiments focused on one-time credit buckets and expiry windows. This introduces cadence (weekly top-ups), explicit anti-abuse lockouts, and an explicit enterprise SQ-to-credits flow tied to contracts and procurement conversation support.
acceptance_criteria: Weekly top-up can be toggled per-customer in Console and via API flag
Lockout rules execute after defined thresholds and change user state to 'top-up-paused' with audit log
In-console CTA surfaces remaining weekly credits and an upgrade action linked to billing flow
Email + in-console drip sent at top-up, 24h before expiry of weekly credits, and on lockout
Metrics dashboard captures cohort-based activation, weekly retention, and upgrade conversion for the experiment cohort
Enterprise SQ flow includes a template clause for contract team and a checkbox in the SQ intake to request boosted credits
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag rollout to 5% of new free signups for 2 weeks; 2) Gradually ramp to 25% while monitoring abuse signals; 3) Open enterprise SQ boosted-credit pilot to 3 Sales accounts; 4) If conversion uplift >= 12% and abuse events under threshold, promote to full free-tier default and add to release runtime-2026.04. Guardrail: immediately revert flag if severe abuse (>=3% of affected accounts cause incident).
